facts.raw_span: A patient with high myopia was examined
The axial length was 30.0 mm
a yellowish oval lesion within a wide area of chorioretinal atrophy
a ringlike low reflectance pattern
a focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina
The sclera was approximately one-third thinner
98, 77, and 50 μm for the pit's floor, temporal wall, and nasal wall, respectively
The choroid was obliterated
Width and depth of 522 × 536 μm
The pit had a homogeneous low autofluorescence
a branch of a posterior ciliary artery near the lesion
The pit was slightly hyperfluorescent in the late frames

concepts.why: High myopia with chorioretinal atrophy and scleral ectasia suggests pathologic myopia.
Focal scleral ectasia with thinning of the sclera is a key feature of this condition.
Chorioretinal atrophy is a common finding in pathologic myopia.
The presence of a branch of the posterior ciliary artery near the lesion suggests an abnormality.
High myopia with retinal degeneration and chorioretinal atrophy is consistent with myopic retinal degeneration.
The presence of a focal scleral ectasia with thinning of the sclera is consistent with a scleral staphyloma.
The presence of a branch of the posterior ciliary artery near the lesion and late hyperfluorescence suggests choroidal neovascularization.
High myopia with retinal degeneration and chorioretinal atrophy is consistent with myopic maculopathy.
The ringlike low reflectance pattern and homogeneous low autofluorescence are consistent with macular retinoschisis.

rationales.F01: High myopia is a risk factor for pathologic myopia and myopic retinal degeneration.
rationales.F02: An axial length of 30.0 mm is consistent with high myopia and pathologic myopia.
rationales.F05: A focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina is characteristic of scleral ectasia and pathologic myopia.
rationales.F08: Obliteration of the choroid is a feature of pathologic myopia and chorioretinal atrophy.
rationales.F11: A branch of a posterior ciliary artery near the lesion may indicate posterior ciliary artery abnormality.
